summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses the laws of Shemirat HaLashon, specifically focusing on when it is permissible to speak about someone who has harmed you. He explains the criteria for speaking for a beneficial purpose (to'elet) and warns against the danger of using these permissions as a justification for revenge or venting. The class emphasizes the difficulty of remaining objective when one is personally involved in a conflict.
questions: Can I speak lashon hara if I am known as a person who only speaks the truth?
Is there a difference between speaking about a sin between man and man versus man and God?
Am I allowed to speak about someone who hurt me if I am doing it to get revenge?
Can I speak about a whole town if they did not treat me well?
How can I ensure my intentions are truly for a benefit and not just to vent?
